title: Check: requests, limits and QoS
description: Five questions on how a Pod asks for and is capped at resources.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a request and a limit?

options.text: A request is a cap; a limit is a reservation
A request is what the scheduler reserves; a limit is what the runtime enforces

questions.explanation: The scheduler only looks at requests when it decides where a Pod fits. Limits are enforced by the container runtime once it is running.

questions.prompt: Which Pod gets the Guaranteed QoS class?

options.text: One with no requests or limits
One where every container sets requests equal to limits for cpu and memory
One with requests but no limits
One with limits on memory only

questions.explanation: Guaranteed needs requests == limits for both resources in every container. Some requests but not matching gives Burstable; nothing at all gives BestEffort.

questions.prompt: The node runs out of memory. Which Pods are evicted first?
questions.explanation: BestEffort first, then Burstable that exceed their requests, then Guaranteed. QoS is the eviction order.

questions.prompt: A container exceeds its CPU limit. What happens?
questions.explanation: CPU is compressible so it gets throttled. Memory is not - exceeding a memory limit means an OOMKill.

questions.prompt: Which object supplies default requests and limits to Pods that omit them?
questions.explanation: A LimitRange sets defaults and min/max per namespace. A ResourceQuota caps the namespace total.
